name: ragg
baseline: Cairo (R grDevices png(type = 'cairo') anti-aliased raster device)
workload: R graphics-device primitives (lines, points, polygons, paths, text, clipping, gradients, patterns) and a layered ggplot2 plot rendered to PNG, timed with bench::mark against void_dev() overhead baseline.
claimed_speedup: README: 'Faster (up to 40% faster than anti-aliased cairo device)'. Performance vignette conclusion: 'a general speed gain of around ~33% compared to cairo' among anti-aliased devices; clipping paths and patterns clearly faster, gradients roughly on par, plain raster blits slightly slower than cairo.
stars_or_usage: 184 stars; on CRAN, widely used as the ggplot2 and knitr PNG device
tradeoffs: R graphics-device package, not a standalone C++ API; the rasterizer is the AGG library (already catalogued as AGG 2.6) wrapped with FreeType/HarfBuzz text and libpng/libjpeg/libtiff output. Always anti-aliases fills, so the win is partly a quality difference.
caveats: Benchmark code is public (vignette) but the numbers are rendered plots; the vignette source does not state CPU or compiler flags (session info is generated at build time). Baseline is R's cairo device, not Cairo called from C++. Gain is smaller where Cairo skips fill anti-aliasing; cairo is faster for opening/closing a device and slightly faster for non-rotated raster blits. The 33% and 40% figures are the author's summary prose, not tabulated numbers. Usable from C++ only by reusing the AGG-based device code, so this mainly counts as evidence that AGG-class scanline rasterizers beat Cairo in an R workload.
found_via: GitHub topic page https://github.com/topics/vector-graphics (C++ filter), surfaced r-lib/ragg; CRAN is the registry

name: NanoSVG2 (RudjiGames fork)
baseline: NanoSVG rasterizer and parser as in the repo's own master before the optimization PRs (nanosvg2 master is derived from memononen/nanosvg)
workload: Rasterizing and parsing SVG files (23.svg, drawing.svg, nano.svg, a gradient test) at 1x and 3x scale with the single-header NanoSVG rasterizer.
claimed_speedup: PR #2: rasterization 2.6x to 3.7x faster (23.svg 1x 15.5 ms to 5.6 ms; 23.svg 3x 83.4 ms to 24.3 ms; drawing.svg 3x 85.8 ms to 31.4 ms; nano.svg 1x 1.29 ms to 0.35 ms), parser up to 2x faster. PR #3 on top: SSE2 blending and fused coverage accumulation, 1.5x to 2.0x faster at 3x scale (23.svg 3x 19.1 ms to 11.1 ms), output byte-identical to the previous master.
tradeoffs: Single-header C SVG parser plus simple rasterizer; SSE2 path is x86-only (a no-SIMD column is reported). Keeps NanoSVG's limited quality and feature set.
caveats: Comparison is between two revisions of the same fork (before and after the PRs), not against Skia, Cairo or Blend2D, and the speedups are only stated against the earlier nanosvg2 master, so the gain over upstream memononen/nanosvg is inferred, not measured. Both PRs were authored by an account named 'claude' on branches under claude/ and merged by the repo owner; benchmark script and CPU are not stated, and the README still says the rasterizer is 'not particular fast or accurate' and the project 'is not actively maintained'. The repo is a standalone copy (initial commit 2024-08-15), not a GitHub fork. Upstream NanoSVG (memononen/nanosvg, registered in vcpkg and Conan) carries no performance numbers.
found_via: WebSearch: 'faster than nanovg OR faster than stb_truetype OR faster than Cairo OR faster than AGG rasterizer C++ repo benchmark' led to RudjiGames/nanosvg2 PR #2; upstream NanoSVG is in vcpkg and Conan
